entities.summary: Henry Jermyn, 1st Earl of Saint Albans was an English politician, diplomat, courtier and property developer. Jermyn sat in the House of Commons of England at various times between 1625 and 1643 when he was raised to the English peerage as Baron Jermyn. Having formed an intimate friendship with Henrietta Maria of France in the 1630s, he constantly devised and promoted schemes to involve foreign powers in English political affairs, both before and after the execution of Charles I in 1649. A long-standing advocate of pro-French policies, he became one of the most influential courtiers of the Interregnum and reign of Charles II.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a key advisor to Charles II and Henrietta Maria of France, Henry Jermyn played a significant role in shaping English foreign policy during the Interregnum, promoting pro-French alliances that had far-reaching consequences for European politics.
